author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: its date and description are changed on the existing visit, validated exactly as booking is, without adding another visit. The correction form is reachable by its own address only; the owner detail page gains no link to it in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit's correction form shows the visit form prefilled with that visit's current date and description
Submitting a present description and a date later than today updates the same visit in place, adds no further visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record
Submitting a blank description refuses the correction and names the description
Submitting a date of today or earlier refuses the correction and names the date
The correction form is reachable by its own address only; the owner detail page carries no link to it in this slice
non_goals: Cancelling or voiding a booked visit (NG-5, cancellation stays out)
Adding a correction link or affordance to the owner detail page in this slice
Any confirmation-message wording on a successful correction
notes: Narrows NG-5 per docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md. Two open questions recorded in the PRD: whether the owner detail page later links to the correction form, and whether a successful correction shows its own confirmation wording. Narrowest reading taken for both in this slice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Conventional Spring MVC edit path in the owner feature package, mirroring the existing create path in the same VisitController and the insert/update branch PetController already uses (branch on BaseEntity.isNew()). No new module, pattern, or integration. The load-in-place question resolves against the existing aggregate model: Owner is the sole write path (system-design Contracts, OwnerRepository row), Pet owns its visits by cascade, and Owner.getPet(Integer id) already demonstrates by-id navigation into the aggregate. The correction updates one existing Visit in place and Owner is re-saved; the cascade persists the update with no new visit row. Verdict minor rather than covered because there is a genuine (small) design decision the author flagged, reflected in a small system-design.md update; not new because no ADR-worthy trade-off exists and every pattern is already present. The non-goal ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md) explicitly admits this correction, so no conflict.
integration_points: GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController; POST reuses the create path's validation (Visit @NotBlank description via bean validation + the non-future-date rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate') check) and redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}

The @ModelAttribute('visit') binding target is the mechanism that makes prefill and update-in-place work: for the edit routes it must return the EXISTING visit (so GET prefills and POST binds onto it), not a new Visit

createOrUpdateVisitForm.html posts to the current request URI (method=post, no th:action) so it already serves both /visits/new and /visits/{visitId}/edit; ${visit['new']} is already false for an existing visit, so no template branch change is required for correctness — treat template edits as cosmetic-only unless a test demands one

patterns.description: existing insert-vs-update branch on BaseEntity.isNew(); the visit correction is the same insert/update shape applied to Visit

Owner.getPet(Integer id) — the by-id aggregate-navigation pattern to mirror; a small Pet.getVisit(Integer id) navigator is the natural home for locating the existing visit, keeping set iteration out of the controller

risks.risk: The pet gains a second visit instead of updating in place — happens if the edit path constructs a new Visit or calls pet.addVisit(...)/owner.addVisit(petId, visit) as the create path does
risks.mitigation: On the edit path, load and return the existing visit from the pet (via Pet.getVisit(visitId), mirroring Owner.getPet(id)); bind the form onto it and owners.save(owner) to cascade the update. Do NOT call addVisit. Assert in a test that pet.getVisits() size is unchanged after a correction (test theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndRedirectToTheOwner)

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit runs before every request mapping in the controller; adding a required visitId path variable to it would break the /visits/new routes
risks.mitigation: Keep the model-attribute method compatible with both route families — e.g. bind visitId as optional and branch (existing visit when present, new Visit when absent), or give the edit routes their own binding target. Either way the /visits/new behavior must be unchanged

risks.risk: A confirmation flash message on successful correction would violate the slice non-goal
risks.mitigation: The correction POST redirects to the owner record without adding a 'message' flash attribute; confirmation-message wording is explicitly out of scope for this slice

notes: No ADR needed: the load-in-place approach is a direct mirror of existing aggregate-navigation and insert/update patterns, not a hard-to-reverse or surprising trade-off; scope is already governed by docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md. system-design.md updated (minor): VisitController purpose extended to booking-and-correction and REQ-VIS-003 wired into the Implements column for VisitController, Owner, Pet, Visit, and OwnerRepository; State Machine note generalized to 'pet and visit workflows' branch on isNew(). No design-doc-autofix records present, so the autofix audit is a no-op. IDE oracle not in this agent's tool list (N/A); resolution claims above are backed by direct Read of VisitController.java, Owner.java, Pet.java, Visit.java, and the template — grep/Read basis, IDE not consulted.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization / parameter tampering: edit routes traverse owner->pet->visit strictly within the aggregate (owners.findById(ownerId), owner.getPet(petId), pet.getVisit(visitId)); a visitId not belonging to the path pet/owner returns null and throws IllegalArgumentException, so a correction cannot reach or corrupt a visit outside the {ownerId}/{petId} in the path (no IDOR cross-object corruption)
id tampering blocked: @InitBinder setDisallowedFields(id, *.id) prevents rebinding the loaded visit or nested entity identifiers via form params

In-place update contract holds: @ModelAttribute(visit) returns the existing Visit instance, @Valid Visit binds onto it, owners.save(owner) cascades the update with no addVisit call on the edit path, so no extra visit row is created
No injection surface: persistence via Spring Data JPA (no string-built queries); description rendered through Thymeleaf auto-escaping (template unchanged)

Mass-assignment on @ModelAttribute Owner is pre-existing and identical to the create-path processNewVisitForm pattern, not introduced by this slice; id/*.id already disallowed; stock PetClinic has no authentication so no per-user authz boundary is bypassed

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The loadPetWithVisit Javadoc is stale in two ways after this change: (1) @return incorrectly says "Pet" — the method returns Visit; (2) the description covers only the original two goals (fresh data, pet has an id) and says nothing about the new visitId-driven branch, which is now the method's most consequential logic. A cold reader consulting the Javadoc in an IDE will see the wrong return type and no hint that the method branches on visitId to return either the existing visit or a new one.
findings.fix: Update the @return tag to "@return the existing Visit when visitId is present, or a new Visit added to the pet when visitId is absent" and extend the description to mention the visitId branching, e.g. add: "When a visitId path variable is present the method locates and returns that existing Visit for in-place correction; when absent it creates and adds a fresh Visit for booking."

approved_aspects: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) faithfully mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer id): same loop, same isNew() guard, same Objects.equals() call, same compId intermediate variable, same null return — verified by Read of Owner.java:117-127 (grep/Read basis; IDE not consulted)

loadPetWithVisit optional-visitId branching is clean: throws IllegalArgumentException on not-found (consistent with existing owner/pet error handling in the same method), returns immediately on success, falls through to the fresh-visit path for booking routes

processEditVisitForm is lean and correct: same validation as the create path, no flash attribute (per non-goals), cascades via this.owners.save(owner) without calling addVisit — no second visit is added
initEditVisitForm and processEditVisitForm follow the zero-argument GET / thin POST pattern established by initNewVisitForm and processNewVisitForm
checkFormat passes (UP-TO-DATE)
Test constants EXISTING_VISIT_DATE, EXISTING_VISIT_DESCRIPTION, and TEST_VISIT_ID are meaningfully named and used consistently across all four new tests
All four new test method names exactly match the PRD test_names list

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Visit object is constructed directly with `new Visit()` in @BeforeEach. Per testing-principles.md: "Tests never call production constructors directly. A slice touching a test moves that test construction behind a factory." The new slice adds Visit construction to this method, so it must use a factory method instead of direct construction.
findings.fix: Extract a factory method, e.g. `private Visit createAVisit(int id, LocalDate date, String description)`, and replace the direct Visit construction in @BeforeEach with `createAVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID, EXISTING_VISIT_DATE, EXISTING_VISIT_DESCRIPTION)`.

findings.description: The bare literal `LocalDate.now().plusDays(10)` is a Tier-2 value (any future date satisfies the constraint; it is not asserted on) but carries no naming that signals its irrelevance. Per the Three-Tier Convention, Tier-2 values use a `SOME_`/`ANY_` prefix or an anonymous factory.
findings.fix: Extract a class-level constant `private static final LocalDate SOME_FUTURE_DATE = LocalDate.now().plusDays(10)` and replace the bare literal in theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDescriptionIsBlank with `SOME_FUTURE_DATE.toString()`.

findings.description: The string literal "Corrected description" appears as a bare literal in two different test methods. In the update test it is a Tier-1 value (directly asserted on) and in the date-refusal test it is a Tier-2 value (any non-blank string satisfies the constraint). Both occurrences are Tier-3 mystery literals until the value is named. The duplication also creates a maintenance coupling.
findings.fix: Extract `private static final String CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION = "Corrected description"` and replace both bare literal occurrences. Optionally use a separate `SOME_DESCRIPTION` constant for the date-refusal test to make its Tier-2 role explicit.

approved_aspects: All four PRD acceptance criteria covered: prefill (theVisitEditFormShouldPrefillTheExistingVisitDateAndDescription), in-place update (theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndRedirectToTheOwner), blank-description refusal, and non-future-date refusal
In-place-update guard present: assertThat(pet.getVisits()).hasSize(1) confirms no additional visit was booked
No domain objects mocked — Owner, Pet, and Visit are all real implementations; ArgumentCaptor operates only on the @MockitoBean OwnerRepository (sanctioned system-boundary mock)
BDD naming convention followed for all four new methods (the{Subject}Should{Outcome})
EXISTING_VISIT_DATE and EXISTING_VISIT_DESCRIPTION are properly named Tier-1 constants
attributeHasFieldErrorCode pattern is consistent with the pre-existing processNewVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture test
Tests pass cleanly with no failures or skips

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction path for a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Contained in the owner feature package: 62 prod lines across VisitController and a new Pet.getVisit navigator, plus 83 test lines and five doc files. Two code modules, no sensitive paths, 28 small hunks.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: the edit path mirrors the create path precisely, returns the existing visit instead of adding one, never calls addVisit, and the date guard !isAfter(now) matches the later-than-today rule. Optional visitId leaves the /visits/new path unchanged. No inverted operator or hidden behavior.

test_adequacy.note: Four tests cover all four ACs with real Owner/Pet/Visit objects; the in-place test captures the saved owner and asserts hasSize(1) plus the corrected date and description, so it would fail if addVisit were called or the wrong instance bound. Assertions target real outcomes, not the implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four final approvals carry empty findings, no escalate tags and no surviving bar_clauses; the first-round autofixes (stale Javadoc, test-constant naming) and the doc CRITICAL (missing ubiquitous-language Correction entry) were all resolved and cleanly re-approved.
